R0274.title: Cross-Modal Injection Attack
R0274.definition: An attack where the attacker injects content via one modality (e.g., vision) to manipulate the VLA/VLM model's understanding of another modality (e.g., text), or vice versa, bypassing single-modal defenses.
R0274.description:
Cross-modal injection attacks exploit the multi-modal alignment space of VLA/VLM — perturbing only the image can simultaneously manipulate the model's understanding of both text and visual inputs. CrossInject performs cross-modal injection via visual-latent alignment and text-guided meta-prompts. CrossMPI perturbs only the image to manipulate text understanding, raising attack success by over 30% versus baselines. VLA-Fool implements unified text/visual/cross-modal misalignment attacks. In the classic typographic attack, CLIP classifies an apple image with "iPod" text as an iPod. Such attacks defeat single-modal defenses (e.g., text-only input filtering), expand the attack surface to any modality, and the optimization focus can shift from the visual embedding space to the model's hidden-state space, with optimal perturbation layers often in the middle of the model.

This risk belongs to the model-layer family together with R0267 (physical-world prompt injection) and R0271 (VLA/VLM adversarial attack); this risk focuses on cross-modal manipulation in the multi-modal alignment space, a key attack path that defeats single-modal defenses.
R0274.influence: Defeats single-modal defenses, expands the attack surface to any modality, and can manipulate model understanding to cause wrong action decisions; the attacker need not manipulate all modalities simultaneously, making defense significantly harder than single-modal attacks.
